options.protects: Avoids an unsafe transfer into an unstaffed bed.
options.risks: One of six resuscitation tables remains unavailable for several hours, with worsening waits, workload, privacy, infection control, and ambulance offload.
options.defensible_by: The emergency lead and ICU clinicians would defend this when the patient requires ICU capability but an empty ICU bed has no safe team.
prerequisites: ICU staff and equipment are brought to emergency and a named clinical team remains responsible.
options.deliberately_asymmetric: Canon gives this pathway patient protection but assigns only capacity and workload costs to persistent state.

options.protects: The new patient enters ICU with a competent nurse and supporting capability.
options.risks: The donating service reduces activity, delays a procedure, or loses recovery capacity.
options.defensible_by: The emergency lead and critical-care lead would defend temporary redeployment because it creates a staffed ICU place without treating a physical bed as capability.
prerequisites: A competent nurse and supporting capability can move from a defined donor service.

options.protects: Internal emergency capacity is eventually released after an accepted clinical transfer.
options.risks: Transport and network capacity carry the burden, and the patient remains under active Bimaristan care during the transfer interval.
options.defensible_by: The city and network coordination representative would defend this when a receiving team and route are confirmed and internal ICU capability is unavailable.
prerequisites: The Regional Health Authority and Emergency Medical Transport Service confirm a receiving team and route.
